framing_issues.text: warns of "upward pressure on base rates."
framing_issues.issue: Uneven verbs: GAM "warns," while PIA Staff "says" in the next sentence. Use "says" for both.

framing_issues.text: and that Georgia Power could have absorbed it
framing_issues.issue: In the 30-second version, GAM's concern is followed by a Staff rebuttal that drops its 2023-2025 look-back framing, so it reads as if Georgia Power could absorb future base-rate changes. GAM's point is rebutted and Staff's is not, and neither Georgia Power's nor GIPL's base-rate view appears. Readers may conclude bills won't rise on the base side.

framing_issues.text: The record also shows that real-time customers pay standard rates
framing_issues.issue: A narrator-voice rebuttal ("The record also shows") placed right after PIA Staff's claim. It is built from Georgia Power's testimony (P-043, P-048, P-052) and does not answer Staff's point, which is about the credit on incremental load, not baseline power. The next sentence merges two different access-charge groups (P-071, P-168). Attribute it ("Georgia Power's testimony says...") and keep the groups separate, as line 75 does.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power says real-time customers already pay "their fair share of system costs,"
framing_issues.issue: Georgia Power's double negatives (P-121 here; P-124 at line 268) are recast as plain assertions, which makes one party's claim stronger than it was filed.
Stated as fact in the narrator's voice, but the only source is Georgia Power's testimony (P-054).

framing_issues.text: The case is about how real-time payments are split, not the prices
framing_issues.issue: Cites Georgia Power's own scope statement (P-133), which GIPL contested (P-136), as the neutral description of the case. P-016 is the neutral source.

framing_issues.text: "should have proposed the associated interchange energy rate."

framing_issues.issue: "Return on Equity" is not explained here. Line 103 calls the same idea a "profit rate" without linking the two terms.
